title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page contains no mathematics. It is a sheet of letterhead from the Università di Pisa, Istituto Matematico 'Leonida Tonelli', with two kinds of content. (1) An Italian vocabulary crib. 'Arrive verci' is a phonetic first attempt. Below it, 'arrivederci' is written in a different, more fluent cursive and underlined with brackets marking syllables or stress groups, as if someone were demonstrating pronunciation. Then comes a bracketed list of courtesy and everyday words: buon giorno, buona sera (with a corrected letter), buona notte, per favore, 'mangare' (sic, for mangiare) and colazione (corrected spelling). (2) A sketch street map. One street is labelled 'Corso Italia'. Near its top end is a small rectangle labelled 'Pizzaria' (sic). Lower down, cross streets are drawn, a small box marked 'V' (perhaps 'via' or a meeting point) and a larger rectangle (a building or piazza). Corso Italia is a principal street in Pisa, so the map is plausibly directions to a pizzeria in Pisa. The surrounding pages (4 and 6) concern the Dieudonné ring A = W[F,V] and its truncations A_n = A/(F^n, V^n). Those pages construct a trace form φ_n : A_n → W_n and the dualizing bimodule I = lim I_n with D(M) = Hom(M, I). This page is an interleaved sheet that ended up in the bundle, reflecting the circumstances of writing (a visit to Pisa around 1969) rather than the mathematics.
errors: 'mangare' is a misspelling of 'mangiare'; 'Pizzaria' is a misspelling of 'pizzeria'. These are ordinary language-learner errors with no mathematical content.

ideas.what: Non-mathematical: Italian phrase list and sketch map of streets around Corso Italia (Pisa) with a pizzeria marked

missed.claim: Biographical/contextual trace: the Barsotti–Tate/crystals notes were apparently written, at least partly, on Pisa Mathematical Institute paper, during or after a stay in Pisa around 1969. Grothendieck was evidently learning basic Italian, possibly with someone else's help: a second hand seems to write and syllabify 'arrivederci'. This may help date the surrounding notes on Dieudonné-module duality, and it bears on Grothendieck's contacts with Italian mathematicians (e.g. the Barsotti circle) during the period when the term 'Barsotti–Tate group' was being adopted.
missed.quote: UNIVERSITÀ DI PISA / ISTITUTO MATEMATICO "LEONIDA TONELLI" ... arrivederci ... Corso Italia ... Pizzaria
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only for historians: it is a small datum for reconstructing the itinerary and dating of Grothendieck's 1969 work on Barsotti–Tate groups and Dieudonné theory. It has no mathematical significance.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is entirely non-mathematical (Italian vocabulary and a street map). Its only interest is as a minor biographical and dating clue linking these notes to a stay in Pisa around 1969.
transcription_corrections: The handwriting appears to come from two hands: 'Arrive verci' (phonetic attempt) versus the fluent cursive 'arrivederci' with syllable/stress brackets underneath. The brackets under 'arrivederci' should be noted.
'buona sera': the first word appears corrected from 'buon' to 'buona', and the r in 'sera' is overwritten. Read simply as 'buona sera'.
'mangare' is as written (sic, for 'mangiare'); 'colazione' is the corrected final reading.

Map labels: 'Corso Italia' is written vertically, and 'Pizzaria' (sic) is written beside a small rectangle at the top. There is also a small box marked 'V' on a cross street and an unlabelled larger rectangle at right.
